questions.stem: In pre-coordinate indexing, when are the concepts of a subject combined into a single indexing expression?

options.A: At the moment the document is indexed — before any user ever performs a search
options.B: At the moment of searching, by the retrieval system
options.C: Only after a user submits a query containing those terms
options.D: When the document is shelved, by the cataloguer

questions.explanation: In pre-coordinate indexing the concepts are combined into a single indexing expression at the moment the document is indexed — before any user ever performs a search.

questions.stem: Why might pre-coordinate indexing be considered less flexible than post-coordinate indexing?

options.A: The indexer must try to anticipate which combinations of concepts will actually be useful to future users
options.B: It only allows one term to be assigned to each document
options.C: It prevents any combination of terms from ever being searched
options.D: It requires every search to use a classified display

questions.explanation: The indexer, not the searcher, decides how concepts relate in advance, and anticipating which combinations will be useful to future users is not always possible with certainty.

questions.stem: Which scholar is closely associated with chain indexing?
questions.explanation: Chain indexing is closely associated with the Indian librarian and classification theorist S. R. Ranganathan; it derives subject entries from the hierarchical chain of concepts in a classification scheme.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of cycling (cycled) indexing?

options.A: To vary the position or focus of terms so each significant component is brought into the leading position, giving several access points to the same document
options.B: To repeat one index entry several times so it appears more often in the index
options.C: To merge two separate classification schemes into a single chain
options.D: To arrange every index entry alphabetically from A to Z

questions.explanation: Cyclic indexing generates multiple index entries by varying the position or focus of terms within a compound subject, so that each significant component is in turn brought into the leading position.

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as an advantage of pre-coordinate systems?

options.A: Explicit relationships between concepts are preserved
options.B: Users never need to understand the indexing structure
options.C: No intellectual effort is required from the indexer
options.D: Search combinations always differ from those the indexer anticipated

questions.explanation: Controlled and predictable representations, preserved explicit relationships, consistent access points and precise subject access are the listed advantages; the limitations include heavy intellectual effort and users needing to understand the structure.
